subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What percentage of the total Edexcel GCSE Music (1MU0) qualification is Component 1: Performing worth?
questions.explain: Component 1 (Performing) carries 30% of the total marks, the same weighting as Component 2 (Composing).

questions.q: How many marks in total are available for Component 1: Performing?
options: 30 marks
50 marks
60 marks
100 marks
questions.explain: Component 1 is marked out of 60, with 30 marks for the solo and 30 marks for the ensemble.

questions.q: How many marks are awarded for the solo performance within Component 1?
options: 15 marks
30 marks
45 marks
60 marks
questions.explain: The solo performance is marked out of 30, and the ensemble performance is marked out of 30.

questions.q: What are the two required types of performance in Component 1?
options: Two solo performances
One solo and one ensemble performance
Two ensemble performances
One improvisation and one solo
questions.explain: Every candidate must submit at least one solo performance and at least one ensemble performance.

questions.q: What is the minimum total combined duration required across both performances?
options: Two minutes
Three minutes
Four minutes
Six minutes
questions.explain: The total time across the solo and ensemble must be a minimum of four minutes.

questions.q: What is the minimum duration required for each individual performance?
options: Thirty seconds
One minute
Two minutes
Three minutes
questions.explain: Each of the two performances must last at least one minute, within the four-minute combined total.

questions.q: On the Edexcel specification, what standard level of difficulty are performance pieces benchmarked against?
options: Grade 1
Grade 3
Grade 5
Grade 8
questions.explain: Grade 3 is the standard level of difficulty against which marks are awarded.

options: A written examination sat under timed conditions
Non-examined assessment, marked by the teacher and moderated by Pearson
A live examination marked by a visiting examiner
An oral viva assessed by Pearson only
questions.explain: Performances are recorded, internally marked by the teacher, and externally moderated by Pearson.

questions.q: Which two elements are the core focus of 'accuracy' in the performing assessment?
options: Pitch and rhythm
Dynamics and phrasing
Tempo and articulation
Tone and style
questions.explain: Accuracy refers primarily to correct pitch and correct rhythm in the performance.

questions.q: Which of the following would be assessed as part of 'interpretation' rather than 'accuracy'?
options: Playing the correct notes
Keeping in time with the beat
Shaping dynamics and phrasing expressively
Reading the pitches from the score
questions.explain: Interpretation covers expressive choices such as dynamics, phrasing, articulation and sense of style, beyond simply hitting the right notes.

questions.q: Why must a candidate's ensemble part be an independent line rather than a doubling of another player's part?
options: To make the performance longer
So the candidate's individual contribution can be clearly heard and assessed
Because doubling is technically harder
To reduce the number of performers needed
questions.explain: The ensemble part must be a genuine individual line so the assessor can judge the candidate's own playing within the group.

options: Playing more loudly than the other performers
Responding to and coordinating with the other performers, e.g. balance and timing
Performing entirely from memory
Choosing a more difficult piece than the others
questions.explain: Ensemble awareness is about listening and responding to others, maintaining balance, blend and togetherness.

questions.q: A candidate performs a piece that is significantly more difficult than Grade 3 standard and plays it well. What is the likely effect on the marks?
options: The marks are automatically capped at a pass
The higher difficulty can allow access to higher marks
The marks are reduced for being too ambitious
Difficulty has no effect on the marks
questions.explain: Because Grade 3 is the benchmark, greater difficulty performed successfully can be rewarded with higher marks.

questions.q: A candidate performs a piece noticeably easier than Grade 3 standard. What is the likely consequence?
options: The marks are unaffected by difficulty
The available marks are reduced because the piece is below the standard
The performance is automatically disqualified
Extra time is added to compensate
questions.explain: Performing below the Grade 3 benchmark limits the marks that can be awarded, as difficulty is factored into the assessment.

questions.q: Which of these best describes a valid solo performance for Component 1?
options: A candidate performing one independent part within a band
Two flautists playing the identical melody in unison
A candidate performing alone, which may include a backing track or accompaniment
A candidate conducting an ensemble
questions.explain: A solo is performed by the candidate alone and may be supported by an accompaniment or backing track.

questions.q: Two clarinettists play exactly the same melodic line in unison throughout their piece. Can this count as a valid ensemble performance for the candidate?
options: Yes, any two performers together form an ensemble
No, because the candidate must sustain an independent part, not simply double another line
Yes, provided it lasts over one minute
No, because clarinets cannot be used in ensembles
questions.explain: Doubling another player's line does not demonstrate an independent part, so it does not meet the ensemble requirement.

questions.q: A candidate submits a solo lasting 45 seconds and an ensemble lasting 3 minutes 30 seconds. What is the problem?
options: The combined total is too short
The solo is below the one-minute minimum for an individual performance
There is no problem; the requirements are met
The ensemble is too long
questions.explain: Although the combined time exceeds four minutes, each performance must individually last at least one minute.

questions.q: A student wants to perform both their solo and their ensemble on the voice (singing). Is this acceptable?
options: No, the two performances must be on different instruments
Yes, a candidate may perform on any instrument or voice, including the same one for both
No, voice may only be used for the ensemble
Yes, but only if a piano accompanies both
questions.explain: Candidates may use any instrument or the voice, and may use the same one for both the solo and ensemble.

questions.q: A candidate plays every note and rhythm correctly but with flat dynamics, no phrasing and a mechanical feel. How is this best assessed?
options: Full marks, since accuracy is all that matters
Strong on accuracy but weaker on interpretation and communication
Zero marks, because expression is missing
Marks only for ensemble awareness
questions.explain: Accuracy is only part of the assessment; a lack of expressive interpretation limits the overall mark.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Music (1MU0) specification; Component 1: Performing
